facts.name: Table Rating Definition
facts.sentence: Table Rating refers to an underwriting classification for substandard risks.

facts.name: Table Rating Multiplier Definition
facts.sentence: Table Rating is expressed as a multiplier to the standard Cost of Insurance (COI) rate.

facts.name: Table D Multiplier Definition
facts.sentence: Table D corresponds to a 1.50× multiplier over the standard COI rate.

facts.name: Flat Extra Premium Definition
facts.sentence: Flat Extra Premium is defined as an additional flat dollar charge per $1,000 of face amount per year.

facts.name: Flat Extra Premium Applicability
facts.sentence: Flat Extra Premium applies to certain substandard risks.

facts.name: No Flat Extra Premium Applied
facts.sentence: Flat Extra Premium is not applicable to this policy.

facts.name: Table Rating vs. Flat Extra
facts.sentence: This policy uses Table Rating instead of Flat Extra Premium.

facts.name: Rating Improvement Review
facts.sentence: Rating Improvement Rider allows for review and potential improvement of the table rating.

facts.name: Rating Review Intervals
facts.sentence: Review of the table rating occurs at specified intervals.

facts.name: Rating Improvement Condition
facts.sentence: Improvement of the table rating depends on health evidence submitted.

facts.name: Streamlined Application Process
facts.sentence: Simplified Underwriting is a streamlined application process.

facts.name: Simplified Underwriting Process
facts.sentence: Simplified Underwriting involves use of a health questionnaire.

facts.name: Simplified Underwriting Data Access
facts.sentence: Simplified Underwriting includes access to third-party data sources such as MIB, Rx check, and motor vehicle reports.

facts.name: No Physical Exam Required
facts.sentence: Simplified Underwriting does not require a physical examination.

facts.name: Impaired Risk Definition
facts.sentence: An Impaired Risk is defined as an insured individual with a health history resulting in a substandard rating classification.

facts.name: Standard COI Definition
facts.sentence: Standard COI refers to the cost of insurance rate applicable to a Standard risk of the same age and gender.

facts.name: Dow Jones Participation Rate
facts.sentence: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (Annual P-to-P) index has a participation rate of 100%.

facts.sentence: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (Annual P-to-P) index has a floor of 0%.

facts.name: Dow Jones Crediting Period
facts.sentence: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (Annual P-to-P) index has a crediting period of 1 year.

facts.name: Fixed Account Current Rate
facts.sentence: The Fixed Account has a current rate of 3.75%.

facts.name: Fixed Account Guarantee
facts.sentence: The Fixed Account has a guaranteed minimum rate of 2.50%.

facts.name: Higher Fixed Rate Advantage
facts.sentence: The Fixed Account offers a higher rate compared to standard products.

facts.name: Higher Fixed Rate Justification
facts.sentence: The reason for the higher fixed rate in the Fixed Account is the older/rated demographic typical of this product.

facts.name: Current S&P 500 Allocation
facts.sentence: The current allocation is 50% to the S&P 500.

facts.name: Current Fixed Account Allocation
facts.sentence: The current allocation is 50% to the Fixed Account.

facts.name: Conservative Allocation Recommendation
facts.sentence: A conservative allocation with meaningful fixed account exposure is recommended due to higher COI charges from the table rating.

facts.name: Conservative Allocation Purpose
facts.sentence: The purpose of recommending a conservative allocation is to provide predictable account growth to offset charges.

facts.name: S&P 500 Cap Guarantee
facts.sentence: The S&P 500 cap is guaranteed never to fall below 3.50%.

facts.name: DJIA Cap Guarantee
facts.sentence: The Dow Jones Industrial Average cap is guaranteed never to fall below 3.50%.

facts.name: Fixed Account Guarantee
facts.sentence: The Fixed Account rate is guaranteed never to fall below 2.50%.

facts.name: Index Crediting Formula
facts.sentence: Standard annual point-to-point crediting calculates credit using the formula: Credit = MAX(0%, MIN(Cap, Index% Change)).

facts.name: Year 1 COI Charge at Table D
facts.sentence: At Table D rating, there is an approximate Year 1 monthly COI charge.

facts.name: Index Crediting Formula
facts.sentence: Credit equals the maximum of 0 percent and the minimum of Cap and Index percentage change.

facts.name: Year 1 COI Charge at Table D Rating
facts.sentence: At Table D rating, the approximate Year 1 monthly Cost of Insurance charge is $260.

facts.name: Year 1 COI Charge at Table D
facts.sentence: At Table D rating, the approximate Year 1 annual Cost of Insurance charge is $3,120.

facts.name: 6% Annual Index Credit
facts.sentence: A 6 percent average annual index credit applies to a $9,000 yearly funded policy.

facts.name: Index Credits Offset Rising COI
facts.sentence: Account value growth due to index credits may partially offset rising Cost of Insurance charges in later years.

facts.name: Regular Projection Review
facts.sentence: Owners should review in-force projections regularly.

facts.name: 0% Floor Protection
facts.sentence: The 0 percent floor prevents negative indexing during market downturns.

facts.name: 0% Floor Protection Mechanism
facts.sentence: The 0 percent floor helps prevent compounding effects from high Cost of Insurance charges during market downturns.

facts.name: Planned Premium Recommendation
facts.sentence: The recommended planned premium is $9,000 per year based on Table D rating and age 59.

facts.name: Higher Premiums for Long-Term Coverage
facts.sentence: Higher premiums than $9,000 per year are strongly encouraged to maintain coverage over the long term.

facts.name: No Contractual Minimum Premium
facts.sentence: There is no contractual minimum premium requirement other than maintaining the policy's non-lapse status.

facts.name: Lapse Risk Above Age 70
facts.sentence: Paying less than $9,000 per year significantly increases the risk of policy lapse after age 70.

facts.name: Maximum Annual Premium Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum annual premium allowed is $30,000 per year.

facts.name: Premium Load Rate
facts.sentence: Premium load is 3.5 percent of each premium payment, applied in all years.

facts.name: Illustrated Funding Assumption
facts.sentence: Illustrated funding assumption uses $9,000 per year until age 80, followed by zero premium payments thereafter.

facts.name: Review Annual Projections
facts.sentence: Policy owners should review annual projections to assess potential account value depletion.

facts.name: Premium Increase Recommendation
facts.sentence: If account value depletion is projected before age 90, owners should consider increasing premiums.

facts.name: Planned Premium Calibration
facts.sentence: The $9,000 planned premium is specifically calibrated for a Table D rating.

facts.name: Premium Reduction with Rating Improvement
facts.sentence: If the policy’s rating improves, the premium needed to maintain the same level of coverage will decrease.

facts.name: Table D Impact on COI
facts.sentence: The Table D rating affects the monthly Cost of Insurance.

facts.name: Table D Rating Improvement Impact
facts.sentence: If the Table D rating improves, the premium required to maintain the same coverage will decrease.

facts.name: Monthly COI Formula
facts.sentence: The formula for Monthly COI is: Standard COI Rate multiplied by Table D Multiplier (1.50) multiplied by NAR divided by 1,000.

facts.name: Table D Multiplier Value
facts.sentence: The Table D Multiplier is 1.50.

facts.name: Table D Risk Multiplier
facts.sentence: The 1.50× multiplier reflects the actuarial assessment of elevated mortality risk due to rated conditions.

facts.name: Guaranteed COI Rates
facts.sentence: Maximum COI rates are guaranteed and included in the policy schedule.

facts.name: Table D Rating Inclusion
facts.sentence: The policy schedule includes the Table D rating in its guaranteed maximum COI rates.

facts.name: Monthly Administrative Fee
facts.sentence: An administrative fee of $12 per month is charged.

facts.name: Guaranteed Administrative Fee
facts.sentence: The administrative fee of $12 per month is guaranteed for life.

facts.name: Illustrated COI at Age 59
facts.sentence: For a male insured under Table D, the illustrated COI at age 59 is approximately $17 per $1,000 of NAR.

facts.name: COI Rate at Age 59
facts.sentence: At age 59, the illustrated COI adjusted by the 1.50 multiplier equals approximately $25.50 per $1,000 of NAR.

facts.name: Illustrated COI at Age 70
facts.sentence: For a male insured under Table D, the illustrated COI at age 70 is approximately $40 per $1,000 of NAR.

facts.name: COI Cost at Age 70
facts.sentence: At age 70, the illustrated COI adjusted by the 1.50 multiplier equals approximately $60.00 per $1,000 of NAR.

facts.name: Illustrated COI at Age 80
facts.sentence: For a male insured under Table D, the illustrated COI at age 80 is approximately $110 per $1,000 of NAR.

facts.name: COI Rate at Age 80
facts.sentence: At age 80, the illustrated COI adjusted by the 1.50 multiplier equals approximately $165.00 per $1,000 of NAR.

facts.name: Illustrative COI Rates
facts.sentence: The illustrated COI trajectories provided are current non-guaranteed rates used for illustration purposes.

facts.name: Guaranteed COI Rate Double Illustration
facts.sentence: Guaranteed maximum COI rates are approximately twice the illustrated non-guaranteed rates.

facts.name: COI Drag at Advanced Ages
facts.sentence: At older attained ages, Table D COI rates consume account value significantly faster than standard rates.

facts.name: Premium Funding & Policy Sustainability
facts.sentence: Long-term policy sustainability depends on consistent premium funding that exceeds the planned amount.

facts.name: Level Death Benefit Amount
facts.sentence: The Level Death Benefit is $250,000.

facts.name: Level Death Benefit Payment
facts.sentence: The Level Death Benefit is payable upon the death of the insured.

facts.name: Terminal Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: An Accelerated Death Benefit - Terminal is available if life expectancy is less than 24 months.

facts.name: Extended Terminal Illness Window
facts.sentence: The extended window for terminal illness eligibility is 24 months, which differs from the standard 12-month window.

facts.name: Extended Window Justification
facts.sentence: The extended window accounts for the common rated risk disease profile of the insured.

facts.name: Terminal Acceleration Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount that can be accelerated under the Terminal provision is 75% of the face amount.

facts.name: Terminal Acceleration Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount that can be accelerated under the Terminal provision is $187,500.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: An Accelerated Death Benefit - Chronic Illness is available when the insured cannot perform two of six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).

facts.name: Chronic Illness Benefit Relevance
facts.sentence: The chronic illness benefit is potentially especially relevant given the medical profile of this insured.

facts.name: Monthly Chronic Illness Cap
facts.sentence: The monthly chronic illness benefit is up to 2% of the face amount.

facts.name: Maximum Monthly Chronic Illness Benefit
facts.sentence: The maximum monthly chronic illness benefit is $5,000.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: The cumulative limit for the chronic illness benefit is 80% of the face amount.

facts.name: Face Amount Reduction Option
facts.sentence: The Face Amount Reduction Option allows the owner to reduce the face amount at any policy anniversary.

facts.name: Face Amount Reduction Lowers COI Charges
facts.sentence: Reducing the face amount lowers Cost of Insurance (COI) charges.

facts.name: Minimum Face After Reduction
facts.sentence: The minimum face amount allowed after reduction is $100,000.

facts.name: Face Amount Adjustment Flexibility
facts.sentence: The Face Amount Reduction Option is useful if financial needs change.

facts.name: Face Amount Reduction Utility
facts.sentence: The Face Amount Reduction Option is useful if lower charges are desired.

facts.name: No Surrender Charge on Reduction
facts.sentence: No surrender charge applies to face amount reductions.

facts.name: Rating Rider Included Free
facts.sentence: A Rating Improvement Rider is included at no additional cost.

facts.name: Rating Review Eligibility Timeline
facts.sentence: The owner may request a rating review three years from policy issue date.

facts.name: First Rating Review Date
facts.sentence: The first possible rating review occurs in November 2027.

facts.name: Rating Review Request – Year 5
facts.sentence: The owner may request a rating review five years from policy issue date.

facts.name: Second Rating Review Date
facts.sentence: The second possible rating review occurs in November 2029.

facts.name: Rating Review Frequency After Five Years
facts.sentence: After the initial five-year mark, the owner may request a rating review every three years until age 70.

facts.name: Rating Review Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: To initiate a rating review, the owner must submit an attending physician statement.

facts.name: Rating Review Submission Requirement
facts.sentence: To initiate a rating review, the owner must submit updated laboratory work.

facts.name: Rating Improvement Based on Health Metrics
facts.sentence: If health metrics improve sufficiently, Inclusive Life may reduce the table rating.

facts.name: Table Rating Reduction Example
facts.sentence: An example of a reduction in table rating is from Table D to Table B.

facts.name: Rating Removal Based on Health Improvement
facts.sentence: If health metrics improve sufficiently, Inclusive Life may remove the table rating entirely.

facts.name: Table Rating Removal
facts.sentence: When the table rating is removed entirely, the rating becomes Standard.

facts.name: Permanent Rating Improvement
facts.sentence: Rating improvements resulting from a successful review are permanent.

facts.name: Retroactive Rating Adjustment
facts.sentence: Rating improvements are retroactive to the next policy anniversary after approval.

facts.name: No Change in Health Metrics
facts.sentence: If health metrics remain unchanged, the table rating remains as originally issued.

facts.name: Worsening Health Retains Original Rating
facts.sentence: If health metrics worsen, the table rating remains as originally issued.

facts.name: No Penalty for Review Request
facts.sentence: There is no penalty for requesting a review that does not result in improvement.

facts.name: Removal of Flat Extras
facts.sentence: Flat extra charges may be removed separately from the table rating adjustment.

facts.name: No Flat Extra Charges Assessed
facts.sentence: No flat extra charges were assessed on this policy.

facts.name: Loan Availability Timeline
facts.sentence: Policy loans become available after year 1.

facts.name: Maximum Policy Loan Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount of a policy loan is 90% of the surrender value.

facts.name: Policy Loan Interest Rate
facts.sentence: The annual interest rate for policy loans is 5.0%.

facts.name: Loan Interest Earnings
facts.sentence: Loaned amounts earn the fixed account rate.

facts.name: Minimum Partial Withdrawal Amount
facts.sentence: Partial withdrawals require a minimum amount of $500.

facts.name: Free Partial Withdrawals Limit
facts.sentence: Up to six partial withdrawals per year are free of fees.

facts.name: Partial Withdrawal Fees After Six
facts.sentence: After the first six partial withdrawals per year, a $30 fee applies per additional withdrawal.

facts.name: Partial Withdrawal Impact
facts.sentence: Each partial withdrawal reduces the death benefit.

facts.name: Elevated COI Structure
facts.sentence: This policy has an elevated cost-of-insurance (COI) structure.

facts.name: Withdrawal Impact on Account Buffer
facts.sentence: Withdrawals further reduce the account value buffer available to cover charges.

facts.name: Account Value Buffer Risk
facts.sentence: Reduced account value buffers increase the risk of policy lapse.

facts.name: Surrender Charge: Year 1 Rate
facts.sentence: Year 1 has a surrender charge rate of 8% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Surrender Charge Rate: Year 2
facts.sentence: Year 2 has a surrender charge rate of 7% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Surrender Charge Rate: Year 3
facts.sentence: Year 3 has a surrender charge rate of 6% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Surrender Charge Rate: Year 4
facts.sentence: Year 4 has a surrender charge rate of 5% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Surrender Charge Rate: Year 5
facts.sentence: Year 5 has a surrender charge rate of 4% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Surrender Charge Rate: Year 6
facts.sentence: Year 6 has a surrender charge rate of 3% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Surrender Charge Rate in Year 7
facts.sentence: Year 7 has a surrender charge rate of 2% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Zero Surrender Charge After Year 8
facts.sentence: After Year 7, specifically from Year 8 onward, the surrender charge rate is 0% of premiums paid.

facts.name: Shortened Surrender Charge Period
facts.sentence: The surrender charge period is shortened to 8 years for this policy.

facts.name: Shorter Surrender Charge Period
facts.sentence: The standard surrender charge period for other products ranges between 10 and 14 years.

facts.name: Shorter Surrender Charge Period
facts.sentence: The shorter surrender charge period of 8 years reflects the impaired risk product design.

facts.name: Older Age at Issue
facts.sentence: The insured person's age at issue is older than typical for standard policies.

facts.name: Annual Free Withdrawal
facts.sentence: A free withdrawal of 10% of the account value is allowed annually.

facts.name: Free Withdrawals Start Year 2
facts.sentence: Free withdrawals begin in Year 2 and continue thereafter.

facts.name: Advance Lapse Notice
facts.sentence: Policyholders receive a 30-day advance notice when there is a potential lapse.

facts.name: 61-Day Grace Period
facts.sentence: There is a 61-day grace period available to pay a sufficient premium after a missed payment.

facts.name: Policy Reinstatement Window
facts.sentence: Reinstatement of a lapsed policy is permitted within 3 years of the lapse date.

facts.name: Reinstatement Requires Proof
facts.sentence: Evidence of insurability is required for reinstatement.

facts.name: Reinstatement Rating Risk
facts.sentence: Due to rated health conditions, reinvestment may lead to the same or a higher table rating.

facts.name: Avoid Policy Lapse
facts.sentence: Owners should make every effort to avoid lapses.

facts.name: Suicide Exclusion: Premium Refund Only
facts.sentence: If death occurs due to suicide within 2 years of issue, only the return of premium applies.

facts.name: Suicide Post-Reinstatement Clause
facts.sentence: If death occurs due to suicide within 2 years of reinstatement, only the return of premium applies.

facts.name: Contestability Period Start
facts.sentence: The contestability period begins on the issue date and lasts for 2 years.

facts.name: Contestability Period Investigation Rights
facts.sentence: During the contestability period, Inclusive Life reserves the right to investigate all claims.

facts.name: Suicide Return of Premium Condition
facts.sentence: Return of premium is only applicable if death occurs due to suicide within 2 years of policy issue or reinstatement.

facts.name: Contestability Period Duration
facts.sentence: The contestability period lasts for 2 years from the date of policy issuance.

facts.name: Claim Investigation Rights During Contestability
facts.sentence: Inclusive Life reserves the right to conduct thorough investigations into all claims for material misrepresentation throughout the entire 2-year contestability period.

facts.name: Simplified Underwriting Without Exam
facts.sentence: This policy was issued via simplified underwriting that did not require a medical examination.

facts.name: Simplified Underwriting Reliance
facts.sentence: Under simplified underwriting, reliance was placed on MIB records, pharmacy databases, and the applicant's submitted application.

facts.name: Undetected Misrepresentation Contestability
facts.sentence: Any material misrepresentation not detected during underwriting remains subject to contestability during the 2-year period.

facts.name: Diabetes Disclosure in Application
facts.sentence: Type 2 Diabetes with an A1C level of 7.8 was disclosed on the application.

facts.name: Disclosed Controlled Hypertension
facts.sentence: Controlled Hypertension was disclosed on the application.

facts.name: BMI 34 Disclosed
facts.sentence: BMI of 34 was disclosed on the application.

facts.name: Table D Rating Conditions
facts.sentence: The disclosed conditions—Type 2 Diabetes, controlled hypertension, and BMI 34—are included in the Table D rating.

facts.name: No Additional Exclusions for Disclosed Conditions
facts.sentence: These disclosed conditions do not create additional exclusions for coverage.

facts.name: Post-Contestability Coverage
facts.sentence: Death from any cause—including diabetes complications or hypertension-related events—is fully covered after the end of the contestability period.

facts.name: Non-Guaranteed Index Credits
facts.sentence: Index credits are not guaranteed.

facts.name: 0% Floor on Index Credits
facts.sentence: A 0% minimum floor applies to index credits.

facts.name: Index Dividend Exclusion
facts.sentence: Dividends derived from index components are excluded from consideration.

facts.name: Table D Rating Cost Increase
facts.sentence: Table D rating results in higher costs for this policy compared to a standard policy.

facts.name: Premium Payment Dependence
facts.sentence: Long-term sustainability of this policy depends on consistent premium payments.

facts.name: Non-Guaranteed Illustrations

facts.name: Guaranteed Illustrations Recommended

facts.name: Standard Annual Formula
facts.sentence: The Standard Annual Formula calculates credit as the maximum of 0% and the minimum of Cap and Index% Change.

facts.name: Uncapped Account Formula
facts.sentence: For an Uncapped Account, credit equals the maximum of 0% and 65 percent of Index% Change.

facts.name: Two-Year Sub-Credit Calculation
facts.sentence: In a Two-Year Sum Account, the first year's sub-credit is calculated as the maximum of 0% and the minimum of 11% and Index% Change in Year 1.

facts.name: Two-Year Sub-Credit Calculation
facts.sentence: In a Two-Year Sum Account, the second year's sub-credit is calculated as the maximum of 0% and the minimum of 11% and Index% Change in Year 2.

facts.name: Two-Year Sum Credit Calculation
facts.sentence: Total credit applied at Year 2 in a Two-Year Sum Account is the sum of the Year 1 sub-credit and the Year 2 sub-credit.

facts.name: Two-Year Sum Cap
facts.sentence: The total credit in a Two-Year Sum Account cannot exceed 22% cumulative over two years.

facts.name: Two-Year Sum Accounting
facts.sentence: A Two-Year Sum Account measures each year's gain independently and applies a cap before summing.

facts.name: Two-Year Sum Calculation Method
facts.sentence: A Two-Year Sum Account does not measure cumulative gain at the end of the period.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Acceleration Definition
facts.sentence: Chronic Illness Acceleration is defined as a living benefit allowing early access to a portion of the death benefit.

facts.name: Chronic Illness Qualification Trigger
facts.sentence: Chronic Illness Acceleration applies when the insured qualifies as chronically ill under HIPAA §101(f).

facts.name: Chronically Ill Definition – ADL Criterion
facts.sentence: An individual is considered 'Chronically Ill' under HIPAA if they cannot perform at least 2 of 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs).

facts.name: 90-Day Duration Requirement
facts.sentence: A loss of functional capacity causing inability to perform at least 2 ADLs must be expected to last at least 90 days.

facts.name: Substantial Supervision Qualification
facts.sentence: An individual may also qualify as 'Chronically Ill' if they require substantial supervision to protect from threats to their health and safety.

facts.name: Cognitive Impairment Qualification
facts.sentence: Severe cognitive impairment is a condition that can lead to qualification as 'Chronically Ill'.

facts.name: Six Standard ADLs
facts.sentence: The six standard Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) are bathing, dressing, eating, continence, toileting, and transferring.

facts.name: Definition of Transferring
facts.sentence: Transferring refers to moving in or out of bed or a chair.

facts.name: Per Diem Limit Definition
facts.sentence: The Per Diem Limit is defined as the IRS §7702B daily limit for tax-free chronic illness benefit payments.

facts.name: Per Diem Limit 2024
facts.sentence: The Per Diem Limit was set at $400 per day in 2024.

facts.name: Annual Inflation Adjustment
facts.sentence: The Per Diem Limit is adjusted annually for inflation.

facts.name: Indemnity-Style Benefit Definition

facts.name: Annual Source of Funds Certification
facts.sentence: Pacific Gateway requires annual source of funds certification from the Owner.

facts.name: Late Documentation Consequence
facts.sentence: Failure to provide source of funds documentation within 30 days of the anniversary request may result in suspension of new premium acceptance.

facts.name: Premium Suspension vs Lapse
facts.sentence: Suspension of new premium acceptance does not cause policy lapse.

facts.name: Maximum Annual Premium Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum annual premium allowed is $100,000 USD per year.

facts.name: Enhanced Due Diligence Threshold
facts.sentence: Premiums exceeding $50,000 per year require enhanced due diligence documentation.

facts.name: Monthly COI Charge Structure
facts.sentence: COI (Cost of Insurance) is charged monthly per $1,000 NAR.

facts.name: COI Calculation Basis
facts.sentence: The 2017 CSO Preferred Male mortality tables are used for calculating COI.

facts.name: Year 1 COI Rate – Age 48 Preferred Male
facts.sentence: Approximate Year 1 COI at age 48 for a Preferred Male is ~$2.10 per month per $1,000 NAR.

facts.name: COI Cost Calculation
facts.sentence: For a coverage amount of $2,000,000 NAR, the estimated yearly COI cost is ~$4,200.

facts.name: Monthly Administrative Fee
facts.sentence: An administrative fee of $15 is charged per month.

facts.name: International Policy Fee
facts.sentence: An international policy fee of $25 is charged per month.

facts.name: Annual Cost Calculation
facts.sentence: The annual cost of 000 NAR multiplied by 2,000 is approximately $4,200.

facts.name: Monthly Administrative Fee
facts.sentence: The monthly administrative fee is $15.

facts.name: International Policy Fee
facts.sentence: The monthly international policy fee is $25.

facts.name: International Policy Fee Justification
facts.sentence: The international policy fee reflects enhanced compliance, reporting, and beneficiary payment administration associated with foreign national policies.

facts.name: COI Monthly Charge Estimate
facts.sentence: The estimated total monthly charge in Year 1 is approximately $350 for COI.

facts.name: Annual Administrative Fee

facts.name: International Policy Fee

facts.name: Annual Charge Estimate

facts.name: Level Death Benefit Amount
facts.sentence: The level death benefit is $2,000,000 USD.

facts.name: Death Benefit Payable
facts.sentence: The death benefit is payable upon the death of the insured.

facts.name: Death Benefit Conditions
facts.sentence: Payment of the death benefit is subject to the conditions outlined in the policy.

facts.name: Death Benefit Disbursement Method
facts.sentence: Pacific Gateway will remit death benefit proceeds in USD via international wire transfer.

facts.name: Wire Transfer Disbursement
facts.sentence: International wire transfers are made to a bank account designated by the beneficiary.

facts.name: Beneficiary Legal Responsibility
facts.sentence: It is the responsibility of the beneficiary to comply with all applicable laws in their country of residence regarding receipt of insurance proceeds.

facts.name: Sanctions Compliance Condition
facts.sentence: No death benefit will be paid if the payment violates U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) regulations.

facts.name: Sanctions-Based Payout Restriction
facts.sentence: A death benefit will not be paid if the beneficiary’s country of residence is under U.S. sanctions at the time of claim.

facts.name: Reporting Threshold for Foreign Payments
facts.sentence: Death benefit payments to foreign beneficiaries exceeding $10,000 will be reported pursuant to applicable U.S. federal reporting requirements.

facts.name: Escrow Due to Sanctions Update
facts.sentence: If the beneficiary’s country of residence is added to OFAC sanctions lists between policy issuance and claim filing, Pacific Gateway will hold proceeds in escrow.

facts.name: Escrow Hold for FATF High-Risk Countries
facts.sentence: If the beneficiary’s country of residence is added to FATF high-risk lists between policy issuance and claim filing, Pacific Gateway will hold proceeds in escrow.

facts.name: Escrow Duration for Country Risk
facts.sentence: Proceeds held due to country risk review may remain in escrow for up to 5 years.

facts.name: Interpleader After 5-Year Escrow
facts.sentence: If legal clearance is not obtained within 5 years, proceeds will be interpleaded in a U.S. court of competent jurisdiction.

facts.name: Escrow Proceeds Holding
facts.sentence: Gateway will hold proceeds in escrow.

facts.name: Escrow Holding Period
facts.sentence: Proceeds will remain in escrow pending legal clearance.

facts.name: Escrow Duration Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum duration for which proceeds can remain in escrow is 5 years.

facts.name: Interpleader After 5-Year Escrow
facts.sentence: If legal clearance is not obtained within 5 years, proceeds will be interpleaded.

facts.name: Interpleading in U.S. Court
facts.sentence: Interpleading will occur in a U.S. court of competent jurisdiction.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Eligibility
facts.sentence: An accelerated death benefit is available for individuals diagnosed with a terminal illness.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Definition
facts.sentence: A terminal illness is defined as having a life expectancy of less than 12 months.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Limit
facts.sentence: The maximum amount payable under the accelerated death benefit is 75% of the policy face amount.

facts.name: Accelerated Death Benefit Cap
facts.sentence: The maximum payout under the accelerated death benefit is $1,500,000 USD.

facts.name: Terminal Illness Documentation Submission

facts.name: Physician Practice Location Requirement
facts.sentence: The physician submitting documentation must practice in the insured's country of residence.

facts.name: Medical Documentation Approval

facts.name: Loan Availability After Year 1

facts.name: Maximum Loan Amount

facts.name: Loan Interest Earnings

facts.name: Loan Compliance Certification

facts.name: Distribution Purpose Verification
